verdict.rationale: Supabase Auth documents that its token scopes database access row-by-row when combined with Postgres RLS policies. Custom Access Token Hooks can inject claims for policy decisions, which gives policy-based, resource-level authorization. However, this relies on writing Postgres RLS policies. There is no documented relationship-based (ReBAC) model or standalone policy engine, and one community member asked which external AuthZ provider to pair it with. Missing for 10: a documented relationship-based authorization model, in-depth first-party docs on policy authoring for fine-grained permissions, and independent hands-on corroboration of complex resource-level authz.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can express fine-grained, resource-level authorization (relationship- or policy-based) beyond simple roles

citations.quote: The Auth Token scopes database access on a row-by-row level when used along with [RLS policies](/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security).
You can use a [Custom Access Token Hook](/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks/custom-access-token-hook) to add, remove or change claims present in the token.
